title: Sophronius, Against Eunomius
english: I also read the attack of Sophronius on Eunomius in defense of St. Basil. His style is clearer and more concise than that of Theodore. He does not traverse all the arguments of Eunomius, but chiefly attacks and refutes those which appear to contain the most essential points of his heresy. The style is aphoristic, the language in general free and simple and not disagreeable, although embellished with over-laboured arguments.
translator_notes: Greek locked from Bekker 1824; Freese 1920 used as PD English reference only.
Codex 5 of 279; Sophronius (fl. c. 400), probably friend of Jerome and translator of his works. 'Aphoristic' = asyndetos (without conjunctions).
Only essential points of Eunomius's heresy refuted; briefer than Theodore.
